text:
Maya: FWIW I sketched a proposal for smoothing the on-demand floor across regions + a separate spot-only burst pool. goal: keep tail latency SLAs while lowering monthly spend. dropping it here for feedback.
Liam: Love the intent. short question: are we talking a static per-region floor or something workload-aware?
Maya: workload-aware. idea is a baseline floor per region (10% of GPU capacity by default) + short-lived burst pools that pull from spot fleets. when a region sees sustained spot churn, we scale the local on-demand floor up automatically.
Erica: How do we detect "sustained"? interruptions over X/min? or queue increase?
Maya: both. trigger if spot interrupts > 5% sustained for 3 minutes OR pod pending time > 30s and queue growth > 10% in 1m. thresholds are configurable.
Sam: Also need to consider cross-region network limits — if we move traffic to another region we hit egress caps and latency. proposal should prefer local on-demand first, then region neighbors only if egress < threshold.
Jon: +1 on guarding egress. lots of past incidents when we shipped heavy KV loads cross-region.
Nina: What about KV cache warming for model runners? switching from spot to on-demand can cost a lot in cold-token recompute.
Maya: Good catch. plan includes a graceful preemptible drain path: before evicting spot node, attempt to transfer hottest KV shards, or checkpoint per-worker state to S3, with priority restore for on-demand re-placements. We also support ephemeral warm-up pods pinned to on-demand to keep a small hot cache.
Erica: That sounds tricky but worthwhile. do we have an estimate on additional on-demand minutes for warmers?
Maya: rough back-of-envelope: keeping 2 warmers per AZ adds ~0.6% on-demand minutes at current fleet size, but reduces cold-start latency by ~40% for replacements.
Liam: How do burst pools work? are they purely spot instances that we accept eviction for, or a mixed binpack?
Maya: burst pools are spot-preferred groups: we prefer spot but maintain a very small on-demand fallback in the pool controller (5% local) to keep jobs running when spot fluctuates for short windows. heavier sustained loss triggers autoscaler-raise on main floor.
Sam: Need operational guardrails: max spend for bursts per account, and a global kill-switch so we can drain bursts immediately during region issues. Also metrics and alerts for when fallback > X%.
Maya: yes. proposal includes: budget cap per-customer pool, per-region emergency drain webhook, and a Grafana dashboard with: spot-interrupt-rate, fallback-rate, avg-pending-ms, on-demand-floor-percent.
Jon: Interruption handling detail: please add backoff jitter and random assignment when re-scheduling to avoid thundering herd on on-demand spots.
Maya: done. also adding exponential backoff with capped jitter and random bin assignment.
Nina: ops runbook? who owns the warmers and the handshake to transfer KV shards?
Maya: SRE owns the warmers, infra runtime team owns the shard transfer protocol. runbook steps included: 1) ops-drain-burst (webhook) 2) check fallback-rate dashboard 3) trigger region-scale action (CLI).
ops-bot: Reminder: runbook link uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/fleet-floor-smoothing (uploaded by ops-bot) :white_check_mark:
Liam: rollout strategy? canary by customer tier?
Maya: rollouts: start with internal + 3 low-traffic customers in us-west1 for 48h. monitor fallback-rate and latency. if stable, enable per-AZ rollouts across us regions, then eu, then apac.
Erica: Cost math? how much savings we expect vs current mixed pools?
Maya: modeled conservative scenario: 12% ops cost reduction from better spot utilization; optimistic 22% if we tune thresholds. net of warmers and checkpoint S3 cost ~ +1.5% so net savings ~10-20%.
Sam: one more risk: marketplace GPUs in eu-central have higher eviction rates. we should start EU with a higher baseline on-demand floor (15-20%). add region profiles to config.
Maya: yep region profiles included. default 10% but eu-central default 18%, apac 12%. all configurable per-customer.
Jon: TL;DR: sounds good. important to keep observability tight and have the emergency drain.
Maya: thanks. next steps: I'll turn this into a short RFC + a prototype controller PR. filing tasks tomorrow. if no major objections by EOD I'll start the RFC.
Erica: Thanks Maya — looks solid, please ping when PR is up and I'll review.
Liam: +1
Sam: +1
Nina: +1
